import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from collections import defaultdict

MAX_DRIVERS = 4

def design(feats):
    # Check if any feature shows significant association with outcome
    p_values = []
    effects = []
    
    for i, fid in enumerate(feats.ids):
        if feats.types[i] == 'clinical':
            # For clinical features, use t-test
            y0 = feats.x[feats.y == 0, i]
            y1 = feats.x[feats.y == 1, i]
            t_stat, p_val = stats.ttest_ind(y0, y1, equal_var=False)
            effect_size = np.mean(y1) - np.mean(y0)
        else:
            # For other features, use correlation
            effect_size = np.corrcoef(feats.x[:, i], feats.y)[0, 1]
            p_val = 1 - stats.norm.cdf(abs(effect_size) * np.sqrt(len(feats.y) - 2) / 
                                     np.sqrt(1 - effect_size**2))
        
        p_values.append(p_val)
        effects.append(abs(effect_size))
    
    # Find features with p < 0.05 (or weakly significant p < 0.1)
    significant_features = [i for i, p in enumerate(p_values) if p < 0.1]
    
    if not significant_features:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Check for near-duplicates (correlation > 0.6)
    correlated_pairs = set()
    for i in range(len(feats.ids)):
        for j in range(i+1, len(feats.ids)):
            corr = np.corrcoef(feats.x[:, i], feats.x[:, j])[0, 1]
            if abs(corr) >= 0.6:
                correlated_pairs.add((min(i,j), max(i,j)))
    
    # Remove duplicates, keeping only one from each pair
    feature_set = set()
    for i in significant_features:
        # Check if this feature is correlated with any already selected
        skip = False
        for j in list(feature_set):
            if (min(i,j), max(i,j)) in correlated_pairs:
                skip = True
                break
        if not skip:
            feature_set.add(i)
    
    if not feature_set:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Select top features based on effect size
    sorted_features = sorted(list(feature_set), key=lambda i: effects[i], reverse=True)
    top_features = sorted_features[:min(MAX_DRIVERS, len(sorted_features))]
    
    # Return design with top features as drivers and all significant as columns
    drivers = tuple([feats.ids[i] for i in top_features])
    columns = tuple([feats.ids[i] for i in sorted(list(feature_set))])
    
    # No products for simplicity
    products = ()
    
    # Loadings based on standardized coefficients
    loadings = {}
    if len(columns) > 0:
        # Use simple linear combination of standardized features
        for i, fid in enumerate(columns):
            col_idx = feats.column(fid)
            # Simple loading based on effect size
            loadings[fid] = effects[col_idx]
    
    return Design(drivers=drivers, columns=columns, products=products, loadings=loadings)
